# Camtek (CAMT): valuation-readiness research, v1
Research cutoff: 18 October 2026. USD millions except per-share values and stated percentages. Unpublished candidate for independent review. Exact equity and current per-share valuations are gated.

## Decision-useful conclusion
Camtek has accelerating demand for inspection and metrology in advanced packaging, but the opportunity brings substantial working-capital requirements and concentrated AI/HBM/customer exposure. The funded operating scenarios produce enterprise values of **$1.22bn / $2.92bn / $4.89bn**. These are scenario outputs, not probabilities or price targets.

The material new information is the October 14 announcement: preliminary Q3 sales of $160–161m, initial Q4 guidance near $180m, roughly $595m for 2026 and an initial 2027 outlook above $800m. Year-to-date orders above $800m cover deliveries across 2026–27; this is **order intake, not an unfilled backlog balance**. Full Q3 closing procedures and results were incomplete at the cutoff. [October update](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326004767/zk2636225.htm)

Capital and discount origin is **June 30, 2026**. Forecasts run July 2026–June 2036 and use information available through October 18, including October market inputs. This is a retrospective-information June-origin analysis, neither an October cash reconstruction nor a point-in-time June investment thesis. Robinhood’s official US page offers CAMT buy/sell; Camtek is a Nasdaq ordinary share with a TASE dual listing, not an ADR. Account-specific permissions are unverified. [Broker](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/CAMT/), [Annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326001561/zk2634678.htm)

## Business and economics
Camtek sells wafer inspection and metrology systems, associated software and services. The mix increasingly favors advanced packaging, HBM, interposers and newer bonding/photonics applications. These application labels overlap and should not be added as separate accounting segments. FY2025 product sales were $468.510m and services $27.562m, only 5.56% of total sales. China shipping revenue was $243.935m, or 49.17%, and the largest customer contributed 11%. Shipping location does not necessarily identify ultimate end use. [Annual financial notes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326001561/zk2634678.htm)

H1 2026 revenue was $254.902m, gross profit $127.631m and GAAP operating income $54.493m. Q2 sales reached $133.243m with GAAP operating margin 20.43%, compared with rounded non-GAAP margin 27%. Acquisition expense, SBC and a $7.7m one-time tax charge complicate earnings comparison. CFO was approximately $3.1m in Q1 and $12.2m in Q2; the sum is approximate because the releases give rounded amounts and no complete H1 cash-flow statement. Receivables of $153.921m and inventory of $116.795m including noncurrent spares show why high sales growth does not translate immediately into cash. [Q1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326002569/zk2635285.htm), [Q2](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326003975/zk2635905.htm)

On the August call, management attributed about three-quarters of revenue to advanced packaging and about half of system sales to newer Eagle G5/Hawk products. It discussed roughly 105-day DSO, rising inventory for production, and further R&D/capacity spending. This is a short paraphrase of a third-party transcription; numeric primary disclosures control. October disclosures supersede the older August outlook. [Call](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/camt/transcripts/666696-q2-2026/)

The October investor model aims for about $1.2bn organic revenue in roughly three years and 34–36% non-GAAP operating margin. Service/software is targeted near $140m, about 12%, with new software sales planned in 2027; that is not established recurring revenue today. R&D rises to approximately $120m, despite percentage leverage. The company explicitly distinguishes this model from guidance. Visual Layer, acquired in April 2026, is intended to support the AI/software program. [October presentation](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326004769/zk2636226.htm), [Acquisition announcement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326002105/zk2635069.htm)

## Ten fiscal years and comparability
Calendar years, source-linked in the companion history JSON. Revenue and operating income for the early years are continuing semiconductor operations after the 2017 PCB disposal. Total versus continuing net income and CFO are separately labeled. Early cash capex may retain disposed-business scope, so CFO less capex is only a diagnostic. Historical balance-sheet capital may include the disposed business.

| FY | Revenue | GAAP op. margin | Continuing CFO | Cash capex | SBC |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | 79.228 | 2.5% | -16.590 | 1.293 | 0.429 |
| 2017 | 93.485 | -3.2% | 12.882 | 3.138 | 0.634 |
| 2018 | 123.174 | 16.3% | 16.791 | 2.243 | 1.681 |
| 2019 | 134.019 | 16.4% | 24.626 | 1.256 | 2.892 |
| 2020 | 155.859 | 14.5% | 25.752 | 2.410 | 4.235 |
| 2021 | 269.659 | 26.3% | 60.957 | 4.065 | 5.815 |
| 2022 | 320.909 | 25.4% | 57.799 | 8.197 | 10.523 |
| 2023 | 315.375 | 20.7% | 79.324 | 8.097 | 12.598 |
| 2024 | 429.234 | 25.2% | 122.239 | 10.102 | 14.501 |
| 2025 | 496.072 | 25.8% | 141.871 | 14.396 | 16.892 |

The 2016 trough includes patent-litigation cash costs and impairment. FY2017 operating income includes a $13m Rudolph patent-litigation settlement; the PCB disposal gain is outside continuing results. FY2019 total net income includes $1.163m of discontinued operations. FRT was acquired in November 2023, so 2024 includes a full-year acquisition benefit. FY2025 net income of $50.722m is depressed by a $100.932m pretax convertible extinguishment loss below operating profit; its 3.1% effective tax rate is not a recurring operating-tax assumption. [Annual filings, original accessions in history file](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326001561/zk2634678.htm)

Data-quality checks found two important issues. First, 2019–25 weighted-share XBRL facts are scaled 1,000 times too small relative to the printed statements. These were corrected with the raw values retained; 2025 diluted weighted shares are 49.970m, not 0.049970m. Second, reported depreciation differs between original and comparative annual notes and does not fully reconcile to 2023 cash-flow D&A. Note 8 also includes lease ROU assets. Reported depreciation is retained and labeled, not silently repaired or described as clean physical depreciation. These limitations do not feed the DCF mechanically: forecast physical depreciation is an explicit 1.7% sales assumption.

Annual 2025 PPE of $65.107m includes ROU assets, whereas the June release separates PPE and ROU. A deliberately approximate closing operating-capital diagnostic excludes operating ROU, retains finance ROU, includes noncurrent inventory and removes financial/tax items. It gives NWC $126.504m and broad capital including goodwill/intangibles of about $285.7m, or 1.74x sales/capital. R&D remains expensed and exact opening capital payables are unknown; this is not economic ROIC. The forecast uses more demanding marginal capital needs and fades returns rather than capitalizing the historical high book return indefinitely.

## Guidance versus actual
- Q4 2025 revenue $128.124m was modestly above guidance of approximately $127m. [Prior guide](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891325003712/zk2533966.htm), [Actual](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326000549/zk2634405.htm)
- Q1 2026 revenue $121.659m was modestly above guidance near $120m. [Guide](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326000549/zk2634405.htm), [Actual](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326002569/zk2635285.htm)
- Q2 revenue $133.243m exceeded $129–131m guidance. [Guide](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326002569/zk2635285.htm), [Actual](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326003975/zk2635905.htm)
- Q3 preliminary $160–161m compares with the earlier $158–160m range. Only revenue is preannounced; no completed GAAP/non-GAAP margin or EPS beat is claimed. [Guide](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326003975/zk2635905.htm), [Preliminary update](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326004767/zk2636225.htm)

The initial base forecast for the twelve months ending June 2027 is Q3 preliminary midpoint 160.5 + Q4 guidance 180 + analyst H1 2027 sales 390 = **730.5**. Calendar 2027 base sales are 820, versus the company outlook above 800. Down/up calendar 2027 assumptions are 720/900; the downcase deliberately misses guidance. Base calendar 2028/29/30 sales are 1000/1160/1300. These are analyst assumptions, not management forecasts.

## Funded operating DCF
Ten explicit twelve-month years follow the June 30 origin. The opening revenue anchor is calendar TTM $509.019m. All margins include fresh equity compensation, R&D and physical depreciation. Cash taxes rise from 12% to 23% as incentives/mix mature; no recurring benefit from the exceptional 2025 tax rate or H1 one-time charge is assumed. Excess-cash interest is excluded from operating income.

| Case | June 2027 sales | June 2028 sales | Terminal op. margin | g / ROIC | Operating EV | Terminal share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| downcycle | 690.5 | 740.0 | 21.0% | 2.5% / 12% | 1,216.5 | 51.9% |
| base | 730.5 | 930.0 | 26.0% | 3.0% / 18% | 2,917.7 | 60.3% |
| upside | 760.5 | 1,040.0 | 28.5% | 3.5% / 22% | 4,887.5 | 66.2% |

Years 1–5 reinvestment is the greater of incremental sales divided by marginal sales/capital or a cash-funding floor. Base marginal sales/capital is 1.45x; physical capex is 3.3% sales, physical depreciation 1.7%, incremental operating NWC 35% of positive sales growth and operating liquidity another 3%. Down/up sales/capital is 1.25x/1.65x and NWC funding 40%/32%. Declining sales do not receive a speculative working-capital release. Any investment above the explicit physical/NWC floor is additional growth-capacity investment; it is not counted again as R&D expense.

Years 6–10 fade investment toward NOPAT × g / ROIC while always honoring the cash-funding floor. Year 10 reconciles to the terminal reinvestment ratio, and terminal investment covers physical replacement, NWC and liquidity. Full annual cash flows and checks are in the model CSV/JSON. Future capex is fully cash funded. Unpaid opening capital additions, if any, are a separate claims gate; the forecast does not gain free supplier financing.

### Discount and return assumptions
Base WACC starts at 10.9630% and fades to 9.7187%. Observed inputs are October 16 US ten-year yield 5.09%, October 1 US default spread 0.22%, raw implied ERP 4.20%, and January 2026 cash-corrected unlevered semiconductor-equipment beta 1.39. Thus the adjusted risk-free/ERP pair is 4.87%/4.42%. [Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026&field_tdr_date_value_month=202610), [ERP](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/home.htm), [Sector beta](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/Betas.html)

Analyst choices are 5% target straight-debt funding, 23% tax shield, 175bp debt spread and mature equity beta 1.15. These are explicit company-risk judgments, not sourced credit quotes. The zero-coupon convert does not imply zero cost of debt. Down/up discount rates are base +125bp/−25bp. Terminal growth is 2.5–3.5%, paired with ROIC of 12–22% and paid-for reinvestment. Lower mature ROIC recognizes competition, expensed R&D, greater scale and the risk that AI spending eventually normalizes. Parallel WACC ±150bp, margin ±200bp and fresh-grant +100bp tests are provided.

### Equity compensation
2025 fresh RSUs and options had aggregate grant-date value about $17.07m, or 3.44% of sales. The model retains fresh economic compensation at 3.8% initially, fading to 3.5%, inside forecast margins. No second future dilution charge is added.

Year-end legacy awards were 649,397 RSUs and 23,909 options; unrecognized RSU cost was $26.088m. June counts, performance/retention awards and option time values are unmeasured. A purely illustrative $8m annual legacy expense is displayed for three years and identically reversed before NOPAT; it has no effect on FCFF. Legacy awards are charged separately through gross units and option value, with no added tax shield. The annual option intrinsic-value narrative and table conflict at $1.338m/$1.388m, neither of which establishes June fair value. [Annual award note](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326001561/zk2634678.htm)

## Dated capital bridge and unresolved claims
June cash $215.229m, short deposits $327.440m, current securities $87.695m and noncurrent securities $185.473m total $815.837m. Reserve $15.271m of operating cash and fund later increases. Common shares are issued 48.760553m less treasury 2.092376m = **46.668177m**. Do not use issued shares or the diluted EPS denominator as current common claims. [Q2 balance sheet](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326003975/zk2635905.htm)

The 2030 notes have $500m face value, June carrying value $488.497m and 4.57275m initial underlying shares. June fair value is not disclosed; December fair value $579.848m is a dated anchor, not a current measurement. The contract permits cash, shares or both. Its initial default is combination settlement with $1,000 specified per $1,000 principal, but the issuer can change the method under the notice provisions. Cash/combination settlement uses 40 trading-day averaging, and make-whole/corporate-action provisions can change shares. This is not an irrevocable cash-principal mandate. [Issuance](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891325003347/zk2533786.htm), [Indenture, section 14](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891325003347/exhibit_4-1.htm)

The model deducts a single full convertible fair-value claim and does not also deduct face value or add all underlying shares. The old 2026 notes had $32.933m principal at December after the costly 2025 repurchase. June carrying value is consistent with only the new 2030 notes, but the interim release does not provide a complete old-note settlement rollforward. This is a gate, not an unsupported assumption that every old note was cash redeemed. June common already includes shares actually issued; historical conversion shares are not added again. No capped-call purchase/contract was found in the reviewed annual and issuance disclosures, so no hedge asset is credited.

June finance-lease and residual tax/acquisition/capital claims are also unresolved. The December finance-lease liability $5.324m is only an illustration anchor. Finance ROU depreciation remains an operating cost and replacement is cash funded; financing interest is outside EBIT. Operating rent remains in margins, so operating-lease liabilities are not additionally deducted. Residual illustrative claims of $25m are an analyst allowance informed by December government/tax payable $12.441m, severance $1.840m, possible tax exposure, and unmeasured opening acquisition/capital liabilities. These may overlap and do not sum to an exact June claim. The $7.7m H1 tax charge is not added a second time, and the $2.482m annual UTB addition is not misrepresented as a closing liability. No deferred-tax asset is credited at book value. [Annual notes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326001561/zk2634678.htm), [Q2](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326003975/zk2635905.htm)

Visual Layer was acquired before the June origin. June cash and operating assets already reflect the transaction. Do not deduct its purchase cash again or credit acquisition cost as an extra asset. Any unpaid consideration/retention claims require separate verification; operating integration cost remains in forecast margins. [Acquisition](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109138/000117891326002105/zk2635069.htm)

The JSON includes conditional algebra assuming convertible value $650m, finance lease $5.324m, residual claims $25m, legacy options $2m and 0.85m gross legacy RSUs. These yield about **$28/$64/$105 per share**, but are **not accepted fair values or price targets**. The $650m claim is unmeasured, not price-fitted, and is held constant only to show arithmetic. Contract-aware scenario claim repricing is still required. Exact equity and current per-share fields remain null.

## Risk and acceptance gates
Watch collections/inventory as bookings turn into shipments, repeat qualifications for new tools, software economics, China shipment exposure, customer concentration, HBM/advanced-packaging digestion, rival offerings and Israel logistics/conflict. A strong demand outlook can still destroy cash if receivables, spares, capacity or compensation outrun margins.

Before acceptance, reconcile June convertible/old-note settlement, gross awards and option values, finance leases and opening tax/capital/acquisition claims; obtain the full interim cash-flow notes; and resolve historical depreciation differences. The operating model is reviewable now, while those equity claims remain explicitly gated. No Atlas app changes or publication have been made.
